cards.title: Comparisons
cards.body: `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `==` (equal) and `!=` (not equal) compare two values. The answer is `True` or `False`.

cards.title: if runs code only when true
cards.body: An `if` checks a condition. The indented lines under it run only when the condition is True. The colon and the 4-space indent are required.
cards.code:
temp = 30
if temp > 25:
    print("It's hot")
print("Done")

cards.title: elif and else
cards.body: `elif` checks another condition when the ones above were False. `else` catches everything left. Only the first matching branch runs.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: x > 0 is False, so Python checks x == 0 next, which is True.

exercise.prompt: Read a whole number. Print `positive` if it is greater than 0, `negative` if it is less than 0, and `zero` otherwise.
exercise.starterCode:
n = int(input())
# use if / elif / else below
